label: Pool Malebo
#why: A widening of the Congo River, a braided ring of channels round Mbamu island: river water, one of the two cases the lake rule's ruling (2026-09-27, by Jens Nordmark (@nordmarj)) names as river water the channel test cannot tell from a reservoir; at elongation 8.7 no width test separates it from a round lake.

label: Nistru
#why: The Dniester's course above the Dubasari dam, joined to the reservoir: a river thread along the border of Moldova's cards, and river water, the second case the lake rule's ruling (2026-09-27, by Jens Nordmark (@nordmarj)) names; its mean width is 0.24 of its greatest only because the reservoir's bulge is in the same lake, so the width test passes it.

label: Margem de rio
#why: A braided river bed in Timor-Leste (Overture Maps water/water, two polygons, 10.05 km2, 501 m at its widest), drawn as a lake line across TL-CO and 13 other Timor-Leste cards: 51.8 widths long but 0.39 as wide along its course as at its widest, as reservoirs are (Komani 44.0 and 0.35, Slapy 40.1 and 0.36), so no width test separates it; river water (ruled 2026-11-12 by Jens Nordmark (@nordmarj)).

label: Lake George (New South Wales)
#why: An endorheic lake that is dry for years at a time, water that is not always there though Overture Maps does not mark it intermittent: OpenStreetMap tags it intermittent=no with surface=grass (read 2026-09-27).

label: Toshka Lakes
#why: Overflow lakes of Lake Nasser, filled only by high Nile floods (1998-2001, 2020) and largely dried out between, though Overture Maps does not mark them intermittent; their 4,205 km2 is a flood extent, not a lake (read 2026-09-27).

label: Lake Fetzara
#why: A shallow depression drained from the 1930s that floods in the wet season, though Overture Maps does not mark it intermittent; the polygon is its winter extent (read 2026-09-27).

label: Hor al-Shuwayja
#why: A seasonal marsh on the Iran-Iraq border, drawn from Landsat imagery at flood, though Overture Maps does not mark it intermittent (read 2026-09-27).

label: Chott Zahrez Chergui
#why: A salt chott of the Algerian high plains; its polygon carries neither the word chott nor Overture Maps' salt flag, so only this exclusion keeps it out (its western twin, Chott Zahrez Gharbi, is refused by name) (read 2026-09-27).

label: Dead Sea evaporation ponds
#why: The salt-works ponds of the southern Dead Sea, a grid of dykes drawn as one unnamed water polygon: salt water no name word or flag catches (read 2026-09-27).

label: Great Vedaranyam Swamp
#why: The tidal salt swamp and salt pans west of Point Calimere, unnamed water on the Sri Lankan cards: salt water no name word or flag catches (read 2026-09-27).

label: El Malaha lagoon
#why: The salt lagoon and salt works east of Port Fouad, unnamed water on the coast: salt water no name word or flag catches (read 2026-09-27).

label: Port of Taichung
#why: A harbour basin (OpenStreetMap landuse=harbour), sea water behind a breakwater, not a lake (read 2026-09-27).

label: Khor al-Zubair
#why: A tidal channel and the port of Umm Qasr (OpenStreetMap water=tidal_channel, water=harbour): an arm of the sea, not a lake (read 2026-09-27).

label: Baie de Saint-Laurent
#why: A sea bay on Monaco's coast that Natural Earth's coastline counts as land, so Overture Maps' sea polygon passed as a lake on MCO's card: sea water, not a lake (accepted 2026-10-22 by Jens Nordmark (@nordmarj)).

label: Caño Tiburones
#why: A marsh and canal reserve near Arecibo, Puerto Rico (OpenStreetMap way w44107088), whose water polygon grew in Overture Maps 2026-09-23.1 to 7.15 km2, 16.0 px on PRI.9_1 - exactly the lake rule's floor - so all 78 Puerto Rico cards drew it as a lake: marsh, not a lake (ruled 2026-10-27 by Jens Nordmark (@nordmarj)).
